slides.title: What HTTPS gives you
slides.summary: TLS encrypts traffic, proves the server's identity and detects tampering.
body: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS. It gives three guarantees between the browser and the server:

ul: Confidentiality: nobody on the network (café Wi-Fi, ISP) can read the traffic.
Integrity: nobody can change it in flight, e.g. inject ads or scripts.
Authentication: the certificate proves you're talking to the real domain.

body: <mark>Many modern browser features (service workers, geolocation, camera, HTTP/2 in practice) only work on secure origins.</mark>

body.note: TLS 1.3 needs only one round trip to set up a new connection, and session resumption can make repeat visits faster still.

steps.caption: The server proves who it is.

item.label: Verify
item.sub: Chain to a trusted CA, name matches, not expired

steps.caption: From here on, all traffic is encrypted.

slides.title: Getting HTTPS right
slides.summary: Redirect to HTTPS, add HSTS, avoid mixed content and keep cookies Secure.

ul: HSTS tells browsers never to try HTTP again; add the domain to the preload list to protect the very first visit.
No mixed content: an HTTPS page loading http:// scripts undoes the protection. Browsers block or auto-upgrade most of it.
Secure cookies: mark them Secure so they're never sent over HTTP.
Automate certificates (e.g. Let's Encrypt / ACME) so they never expire unnoticed.

body: <mark>Without HSTS, the first plain-HTTP request can be intercepted and the user kept on a fake HTTP version of your site.</mark>

viz.html: upgrade-insecure-requests in your CSP rewrites leftover http:// subresource URLs to https://.
